answer: Keep the checker fixed and separate from the writer, and have someone spot-check it by hand, because the score is only worth trusting if the yardstick never moves. Even then, a passing check only proves the work is sourced, not that it's good, and deciding what good means stays with us.
claims: When you use an automated check to grade work, keep that check unchanged and run by something other than whoever produced the work, and have a person occasionally review its results by hand, so the scores stay comparable over time.
Don't let the same author who wrote the content also run or adjust the grader; freeze the grading setup and have a human manually sample its verdicts to confirm it still works.
A passing score only tells you the work cites its sources, not that it's good, so people still have to decide what counts as good quality and not hand that call to the checker.
Set up a fixed, independent grader with human hand-checks so scores can be trusted, but remember a pass only shows the work is sourced; humans must still define and judge quality.
